name: Apache Cassandra
model: Tables queried with CQL (SQL-like, no joins); rows grouped into partitions by partition key and sorted by clustering columns
engine_note: LSM tree: commit log plus memtable, flushed to immutable SSTables merged by compaction; every node equal, no leader
consistency: Tunable per query (ONE, QUORUM, ALL); default ONE, so reads can be stale. Writes within one partition are atomic and isolated; logged batches eventually all apply. Lightweight transactions (Paxos) give linearizable compare-and-set. Commit log fsync every 10 s by default.

jepsen.finding: Last-write-wins by timestamp silently lost acknowledged writes even at strong levels, counters drifted, and early lightweight transactions lost writes; LWT bugs were later fixed, timestamp semantics are by design.

scaling: Add nodes: data is spread automatically by hashing the partition key around a token ring, with replicas in several racks or data centres; scales writes nearly linearly.
managed: Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra
version_note: Download page shows 5.0 latest release 2026-08-07 (5.0.9). 6.0 is in alpha (6.0-alpha2 tag) and brings Accord multi-partition ACID transactions; not GA.
reach: Reach for it when you need very high write throughput across many machines or data centres, always-on availability, and you query by known partition keys.
avoid: Avoid when you need joins, ad hoc queries, multi-row transactions across partitions, or strong consistency by default; also when data fits one Postgres server.
escape: Writes outgrow one machine and you need multi-datacentre, always-writable storage keyed by partition.
chat: Message history partitioned by chat id, at very large scale (Discord-style); overkill for most apps.
notes: Version date: download page says latest 5.0 release 2026-08-07, while the cassandra-5.0.9 tag commit is 2026-07-28 (vote period); used the page date. Default consistency level ONE for cqlsh and most drivers (driver dependent). Commit log default commitlog_sync: periodic with 10000 ms period per cassandra.yaml in 5.0.9, so a whole-cluster power loss can lose recent acknowledged writes; batch/group modes fsync before ack. Amazon Keyspaces is an AWS-built Cassandra-compatible service, not Cassandra.
